origin.public_summary: Candidate profile: Aras, a 45-year-old human field-cartographer with decades of adult work behind him — route surveys, map commissions, long seasons of field observation — now at home in a district he knows intimately, with an unfinished regional map and a rumor he has only heard secondhand.

life_facts.fact: Aras is 45 years old and has spent roughly two decades of adult life on field exploration and map sketching.
He is patient by temperament, willing to walk a route several times before committing a line to paper.
He keeps careful notes — field journals, margin annotations, dated observations — a habit built over years of professional work.
His working territory is his home district and the surrounding region, which he has come to know through repeated, methodical travel.
He knows the COMMONS_DISTRICT as a discovered place — a hub where he has gathered talk, commissions, and secondhand accounts over the years.
He has heard secondhand talk of an OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL but has never visited it and holds no confirmed route or interior knowledge of it.

formative_events.event: As a young adult, Aras spent several seasons as an assistant on long route surveys, learning that a map is only as trustworthy as the patience behind it.
formative_events.character_takeaway: Accuracy is earned by repetition, not rushed by ambition.

formative_events.event: Early in his independent career, one of his drafted maps contained a route error that misled a traveler; he corrected it publicly and rebuilt his method around double-checking.
formative_events.character_takeaway: A cartographer's errors are not private — they can cost others.

formative_events.event: A multi-year effort to chart the back routes of his home region became his life's working project — one he has never considered finished.
formative_events.character_takeaway: A region is never fully mapped; the work is a long conversation, not a conclusion.

formative_events.event: A long working partnership with a fellow field-worker ended when their paths diverged — the parting was civil but left a collaboration unfinished.
formative_events.character_takeaway: Even good working relationships can leave loose ends that outlast the parting.

prior_roles.role: Survey assistant on regional route-mapping crews
prior_roles.responsibility: Pacing distances, recording bearings, and maintaining the field journals that senior cartographers relied on.
Producing reliable route sketches and written observations for clients who needed trustworthy descriptions of the surrounding region.

prior_activities.activity: Repeated field exploration walks through the home district and surrounding region, logging routes over many years.
Map sketching and revision — drafting, correcting, and annotating route drawings from field notes.
Route observation — timing walks, noting landmarks, and comparing older accounts against what he actually finds.
Gathering secondhand accounts and local talk in the COMMONS_DISTRICT to cross-check his own observations.

meaningful_people.relationship_seed: A senior cartographer who trained Aras in field discipline decades ago; the relationship shaped his standards but has since lapsed into long silence.
A fellow field-worker with whom Aras shared years of route surveys; their working partnership ended amicably but with an unfinished joint project between them.
A merchant or official who has commissioned route sketches from Aras over the years — a professional trust built on delivered, accurate work.

unresolved_questions.question: Will Aras ever finish his definitive map of the home region, or is the region's constant small change an argument that the work can never truly close?
unresolved_questions.knowledge_boundary: He knows his own decades of notes; he cannot know whether the region has changed beyond what he has personally re-checked.

unresolved_questions.question: What became of the unfinished joint survey he and his former field partner set aside years ago?
unresolved_questions.knowledge_boundary: He knows the project was left incomplete; he does not know whether his old partner ever continued it alone.

unresolved_questions.question: Is the secondhand talk of an OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL worth following up on, or is it just local hearsay that will not survive his standards of verification?
unresolved_questions.knowledge_boundary: He has only hearsay-level awareness; he has no confirmed route, no firsthand sighting, and no reliable account of what the trail actually contains.

saga.public_premise: A 45-year-old field-cartographer stands at mid-life with a body of work behind him and an unfinished regional map before him. His long-horizon tension is between the desire to complete a definitive record and the humbling reality that territory, talk, and time keep moving — with one unverified rumor, the OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL, sitting at the edge of his hearsay knowledge.

long_horizon_tensions.tension: Completion versus change: Aras wants a finished, trustworthy map of his region, but every season the routes shift a little and the map ages the moment it is drawn.
Verification versus hearsay: his professional standard is firsthand confirmation, yet some of the most interesting material — like the rumored OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL — reaches him only as secondhand talk.
Independence versus unfinished partnership: he built his career on self-reliant fieldwork, but his most significant old collaboration was never completed, and the loose end has lasted years.

known_truth_proposals.statement: Aras is 45 years old and currently at HOME, a location he knows at the EXPLORED level.
Aras knows the COMMONS_DISTRICT at the DISCOVERED level.
Aras's awareness of the OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL is RUMORED — hearsay-level only, with no visit, no interior knowledge, and no confirmed route.

belief_proposals.statement: Aras believes careful notes outlast memory and that a route is not known until it has been walked and recorded more than once.
Aras believes every route deserves recording, even the humble ones, because today's minor path may be tomorrow's important way.
Aras believes hearsay is a starting point for questions, never a substitute for firsthand observation.

reveal_constraints: OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL must remain hearsay-level: no confirmed route, no interior detail, no claim of visitation, and no firsthand content may be introduced through this saga.
No magic, supernatural abilities, or impossible technology; ordinary everyday physics only.
No new canonical locations may be created beyond the supplied known_locations keys.
All prior-life history remains candidate-only and must not be committed as canon.
No named NPC identities may be introduced; relationships stay role-only and unbound.

safe_breadcrumbs.breadcrumb: Aras's field journals contain decades of dated route observations, including older entries whose routes he has not re-verified in years.
His unfinished regional map has blank margins in the directions he has surveyed least thoroughly.
Talk he has heard in the COMMONS_DISTRICT includes secondhand mentions of an old quarry trail — accounts that conflict with one another and none of which he has verified.
Among his papers is the incomplete draft of the joint survey he and his former field partner set aside, its final sections never filled in.

The lapsed relationship with his former surveying mentor, and whether the long silence between them could be broken.

The unverified hearsay about the OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL — whether it will remain rumor or ever become something Aras can properly investigate.

All prior-life content (roles, events, people, questions) remains candidate-only and may be revised or discarded without contradiction.
Relationships are role-only and unbound; if existing NPCs are later bound, they must remain compatible with the role seeds, not the reverse.
Any future breadcrumb about the OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL must stay at hearsay level and must not attribute firsthand knowledge to Aras.
Aras's method — patient, note-keeping, verification-first — should remain consistent across any future materialization.

memories.memory_summary: The early seasons as a survey assistant — long walks, aching feet, and the first time a route he had paced matched the senior cartographer's figures exactly.
The route error in one of his early independent maps that misled a traveler, and the public correction he made afterward.
A hard field season in the surrounding region — bad weather, slow progress, and the patient decision to turn back and re-walk the route another year rather than record it half-seen.
The day he and his field partner set their joint survey aside — a calm conversation, a handshake, and a draft that was never finished.
Hearing secondhand talk in the COMMONS_DISTRICT about an old quarry trail — conflicting accounts he noted down as hearsay, never verified.

origin_threads.thread: The unfinished definitive map of the home region — a standing question of what to re-verify next, not a task with a fixed endpoint.
The lapsed silence with his former surveying mentor — an old relationship that could be re-opened but has no obligation attached.

candidate_goals.goal: Resume work on the unfinished regional map, starting with the sections whose observations are oldest and least re-verified.

candidate_concerns.concern: Some of his older route observations may no longer match the actual paths, and he cannot know which until he re-walks them.
The rumored OLD_QUARRY_TRAIL tempts his curiosity, but acting on unverified hearsay conflicts with the professional standards that built his reputation.
At 45, he is aware that the routes he can comfortably re-walk each season may slowly narrow, and his map may need to outlast his own fieldwork.
